newsitem.title: JAPAN: Apollo to ask Sakura Bank to support restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Apollo to ask Sakura Bank to support restructuring.

text.p: An executive at Japanese non-bank financial institution Apollo Leasing Co said on Monday the company would keep asking Sakura Bank Ltd, a major creditor of Apollo, to support a rehabilitation plan the firm has worked out.
The executive told reporters Apollo did not have any plan to change the content of the restructuring proposal.

Earlier on Monday, a Sakura spokesman said the bank had told Apollo "it would be difficult to agree" to the restructuring plan. The spokesman said that under the plan, Apollo was calling on creditors to waive 50 percent of their balance of loans, with remaining claims and debts to be written off by revenues from performing assets.
The spokesman did not make any further comment.

Apollo Leasing extended loans to real estate firms during the bubble economy in the late 1980s. But like many small and medium-sized financial institutions it was sent into a tailspin by the collapse of the asset-price bubble in the early 1990s.
The Apollo executive said about two-thirds of the 355.4 billion yen in its loans outstanding at the end of March last year was estimated to be non-performing.
He said that under the plan, Apollo was calling on creditors to waive 245 billion yen out of 490 billion yen of their loans outstanding to Apollo.

The company planned to pay back 195 billion yen through disposing of collateral and to regard the remaining 50 billion yen as assets relating to Apollo's leasing and other financing business, he said.

The executive said Sakura had rejected the restructuring plan as the amount which creditors must waive was very large. Sakura also pointed to difficulty of raising 195 billion yen through disposal of collateral, he said.
"We are asking Sakura to help dispose of collateral," he said.
